newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank, Barnett close to expectations.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank, Barnett close to expectations.

text.p: Fourth-quarter earnings at NationsBank Corp and Barnett Banks Inc, reported on Monday, were close to expectations, reflecting solid industry fundamentals, analysts said.
"They were good numbers for both companies," said Anthony Davis, an analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds.
Ruchi Madan, analyst at Prudential Securities, said the numbers were "pretty much in line" with her estimates.
Barnett, which sold $776 million of non-core credit card loans to Household International Inc during the quarter, saw its fourth quarter credit card charge-offs fall sharply as a result.

For the fourth quarter, Jacksonville, Fla.-based Barnett reported that earnings rose 13 percent from a year ago to $0.76 per share. The consensus estimate on Institutional Brokers Estimate System was $0.74 per share.
Fourth-quarter earnings at NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., got a boost from bond trading and investment banking results.
"Overall, it was a damn good quarter," Davis said of the NationsBank results.
NationsBank earned $2.14 per diluted share in the quarter, compared to a consensus estimate of $2.11 per share in data compiled by the Institutional Brokers Estimate System.

NationsBank, following the close of its quarter, completed its acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc of St. Louis, a move that lifts NationsBank from its ranking as fifth largest bank in the U.S., based on assets, into fourth place with about $227 billion in assets.

NationsBank said net interest income rose to $1.612 billion in the fourth quarter from $1.438 billion a year ago. The net interest margin rose to 3.75 percent from 3.38 percent a year ago. Overall, fourth-quarter net income rose 24 percent to $632 million.
Analysts said credit quality at both NationsBank and Barnett was good.
NationsBank was off 1-1/8 to 101-7/8 in afternoon trade, and Barnett was up 1/8 to 40-3/4.
